text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Fifteen percent of Vietnam's state budget will be earmarked by the year 2000 for investment in education and training.

-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has indicated Vietnam's intention of requesting further economic development assistance from France. Speaking to France's new ambassador to Hanoi, Serge Degallaix, Kiet said Hanoi was hoping for assistance in health care and pharmaceutical production, in regional tourism development and in mechanisation of the agriculture industry.

-- The 1997 budget deficit will not exceed 3.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) while the state budget is expected to increase by 12.2 percent, Finance Minister Nguyen Sinh Hung said. Thrift will be the buzzword of the ministry next year, with belt-tightening in consumption and production.
-- The inflation rate for the whole year has been estimated at 4.5 percent, with the price index for this month up one percent from November.
-- International calls for every three minutes from Vietnam will be between 5.02 and 23.46 percent cheaper from January 1.
-- Vietnam's former acting President and former Chairman of the National Assembly, Nguyen Huu Tho, died on Tuesday in Ho Chi Minh city at the age of 86.
-- France's ambassador to Hanoi told Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet that French President Jacques Chirac has accepted an invitation to visit Vietnam next year.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi and Yatsushi Kitani, a member of the Central Committee of Japan's Communist Party, held talks on strengthening cooperation between the two parties.
-- Politburo member Le Duc Binh has called on Voice of Vietnam radio to improve its broadcasting programme.
-- The Vietnam Post and Telecommunication Corporation has announced a reduction in the cost of international telephone calls which will come into effect from January 1, 1997.
